extraction.name: VoiceAssistant-Eval
extraction.description: A comprehensive benchmark designed to assess AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing. It comprises 10,497 curated examples spanning 13 task categories, including natural sounds, music, and spoken dialogue for listening; multi-turn dialogue, role-play imitation, and various scenarios for speaking; and highly heterogeneous images for viewing.
extraction.creator: Ke Wang, Houxing Ren, Zimu Lu, Mingjie Zhan, Hongsheng Li
extraction.citeAs: Wang, K., Ren, H., Lu, Z., Zhan, M., & Li, H. (2025). VoiceAssistant-Eval: Benchmarking AI Assistants Across Listening, Speaking, and Viewing. arXiv preprint arXiv:2509.22651.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Visual and auditory inputs are extracted and adapted from 47 datasets (spanning natural sounds, music, dialogue, and varied images). For voice personalization, texts are gathered from RoleBench across 100 distinct roles with 3 representative audio clips per role. Question texts are preprocessed and synthesized into speech using three TTS models (F5-TTS, ChatTTS, and Dia-1.6B). A four-stage curation pipeline (deduplication, validation, categorization, and sampling) is then applied.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Approximately 10% of candidate items are removed during validation due to corrupted images, silent or broken audio, ill-posed prompts, and demonstrably incorrect answers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Extracted from 47 open/academic source datasets including MMMU, VocalBench, AlpacaEval, MMSU, RoleBench, AdvBench, AIR-Bench, MEAD, BeaverTails-Eval, MT-Bench-101, VCTK, IFEval, MusicCaps, CommonVoice, SD-Eval, Nsynth, BIG-Bench Hard, Clotho, SLURP, VoiceBench, MTG-Jamendo, JL Corpus, MELD, AudioCaps, AudioGrounding, CoVoST 2, LibriSpeech, VocalSound, VoxCeleb1, MUSIC-AVQA, FoR, SpeechInstructBench, IEMOCAP, FollowBench, SpokenWOZ, TUT2017, AVQA, CommonsenseQA, GSM8K, STORAL, Clotho-AQA, FMA, CochlScene, Fisher, MT Bench, RAVDESS, and MyST.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Texts are preprocessed for TTS: special tokens referencing images are replaced with descriptive phrases (e.g., '<image1>' to 'as shown in the first image'), Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct is used to rewrite texts into phonetically clear expressions (e.g., mathematical formulas and numbers written out), and multiple-choice options are rephrased for readability. Synthesized speech from F5-TTS, ChatTTS, and Dia-1.6B is scored with UTMOS Strong (regenerated if score < 3.8) and transcribed using Whisper-Large-v3 to select the candidate with the lowest word error rate. Questions are deduplicated using lexical overlap and Levenshtein distance matching.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Candidate items are reviewed by human curators using a lightweight web-based curation tool across three passes: (1) Media integrity (verifying audio/images are present, decodable, audible, visible, and not silent or corrupted), (2) Task well-posedness (confirming the prompt is unambiguous and matches inputs), and (3) Answer validity (checking reference answers are consistent with prompt and media, and multi-turn items are coherent). Curators assign Good/Bad verdicts and logs are exported. For automated benchmark evaluation, responses are scored on content quality by gpt-oss-20b using 13 task-specific prompts, speech naturalness by UTMOS, and consistency by a modified Word Error Rate via Whisper-Large-v3, alongside Wespeaker for speaker similarity.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: A lightweight web-based curation tool developed by the authors featuring inline media players, image viewers, transcripts, and decision logging.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Agreement between automated evaluator gpt-oss-20b and human judges was validated on 1,050 sampled responses across all 13 tasks, yielding Pearson correlation coefficients between 0.73 and 1.00 (overall 0.92) and an overall human agreement rate of 96.1%. Stability tests across 10 repeated runs showed high consistency with low standard deviations (mostly below 3).
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: F5-TTS, ChatTTS, Dia-1.6B, UTMOS Strong, Whisper-Large-v3, Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, gpt-oss-20b, emotion2vec, Wespeaker
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors maintain a data governance process for auditing and removal, and reserve the right to update assets if consent or licensing concerns arise.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Role audio profiles representing specific roles/speakers, user emotions (7 classes), and vocal timbre. The paper explicitly addresses identity spoofing, impersonation, fraud, and privacy risks associated with voice cloning.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Enables evaluation of hands-free and voice-first AI assistants for accessibility (e.g., visually impaired users, hands-free driving, operating machinery), healthcare, smart homes, customer service, and education. Identifies safety risks, misalignment, and vulnerabilities to jailbreaks/misuse (impersonation, harassment, fraud).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The benchmark relies heavily on English prompts and evaluations (with only five Chinese roles in the role-play task), carrying a monolingual focus. The role-play subset uses a fixed set of 100 roles and style prompts that may encode stereotypes or omit important user personas. Contexts and questions drawn from academic or synthetic sources may introduce source-domain biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Monolingual bias (mostly English); evaluated across only a single proprietary model (GPT-4o-Audio) due to cost/access; relies partly on automated GPT judges which may carry phrasing bias; lacks continuous audio-visual streaming or video-audio integration; evaluated in an offline, static manner without capturing real-time operational factors such as latency, barge-in/interruption, and error recovery.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating AI assistants across listening, speaking, and viewing capabilities. Intended for evaluation/testing and research purposes; not intended to be used for training models for cheating. Downstream use requires strict anti-impersonation safeguards, consent gating, and synthetic audio watermarking/traceability.
